Messages.Author: Morgan Vening
Messages.Body:
Regarding GtU, 4th Tradition, Enchant Kindred, etc. that explicitly
state "to a YOUNGER vampire", how is that handled with regards proving
it's youth? Do you have to reveal the vampire's capacity? Mark it as
"Below X" or what? The rules don't seem to cover this in any
meaningful way.

Morgan Vening

Messages.Author: salem
Messages.Body:
On Fri, 14 May 2004 14:45:13 +1000, Morgan Vening

in social play: trust. or make a note, and check it when the vampire
enters play, or the game ends, or something.

Messages.Author: Hardy Range
Messages.Body:
Morgan Vening <mor...@optusnet.com.au> wrote in message news:<8oe8a0t1e265hr1gc...@4ax.com>...


Hello Morgan,

you cannot reveal the vampire, since that is explicitly forbidden by
the Tournement Rules.

The usual solution would be to call the Judge when in doubt; her or
she can then verify that the Govern has been used on a legal target.

Regards,

Hardy Range
Prince of Bochum, Germany

Messages.Author: Daneel
Messages.Body:
Morgan Vening <mor...@optusnet.com.au> wrote in message news:<8oe8a0t1e265hr1gc...@4ax.com>...



IANLSJ, but I'd say that in tournament play you may simply ask a judge
or assistant judge to confirm. In non-tournament play you can always
ask a bystander to confirm, but you will probably see the vampire soon
anyway (if it is influenced out).

Bye,

Daneel
